text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today after releasing quarterly earnings on November 3rd, capping a volatile two-week stretch down 9.7%. The stock has swung sharply—jumping to $444.73 just three days ago before retreating—suggesting investors are weighing the company's earnings results against uncertainty about refining margins and geopolitical risk. US oil at $103 per barrel remains well above historical averages, but the gap between global oil ($123) and domestic prices signals some strain on refining profitability.

The broader backdrop of caution around Big Oil earnings (noted in late October coverage) and a recent leadership change at Marathon may be adding to the hesitation, even as refineries run near full capacity at 92.8%. Geopolitical tensions with Iran also add an overlay of uncertainty to energy markets that could affect crude supplies and refining economics going forward.
